A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VITA-1.5, with readable text, figures, tables, and references supporting a reliable comparison. All 13 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v4 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Tables 2–4 report original VITA-1.5 evaluations on image understanding, video understanding, and Mandarin/English speech recognition, including comparisons between training stages.

after.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the work's original image, video, and speech-recognition results. Retaining these results still establishes original empirical content.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same encoders, adapters, NAR/AR speech decoders, CTC alignment, and three-stage training procedure. Although Figure 3 omits some annotations in v4, its state head and module trainability remain explicitly specified in Section 3.3.2; no changed procedure is stated.

E1.justification: Table 1 and Section 4 retain the same training datasets, Chinese/English coverage, and image, video, and ASR evaluation tasks. Personalization and long-duration interaction are proposed as future work, not newly evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within Tables 2–4. Mini-Omini2 and Freeze-Omini become Mini-Omni2 and Freeze-Omni through spelling corrections. Newly discussed models such as LLaMA-Omni and Moshi are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported image preprocessing, video-frame sampling, training-data quantities and sampling ratios, model configurations, evaluation splits, and CER/WER metrics are unchanged. No additional evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The Stage 1 versus Stage 3 visual-capability comparisons in Tables 2–3 and the demonstration in Figure 1 are retained. Neither new ablations nor additional robustness, sensitivity, error, or case analyses appear.

E5.justification: Both versions report point scores without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All scores and result rows in Tables 2–4 match. For example, the Stage 3 image average remains 66.8, Video-MME without subtitles remains 56.1, and AISHELL-1 CER remains 2.2. The reported qualitative findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The qualitative training rationale and reference to the CTC objective are retained without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: Both versions claim unified vision/speech interaction through staged training, preservation of visual capabilities, and efficient speech output without separate ASR/TTS modules. The abstract's revised 'omni' wording does not change these contributions; near-real-time interaction remains claimed elsewhere.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly acknowledges the absence of personalization and identifies long-term memory for extended interactions as future work. These add concrete applicability limitations, while interpretations of the benchmark results and modality-conflict mitigation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Architecture dimensions, codec settings, data-processing instructions, and training-data disclosures are retained. The source-code and demonstration link targets are unchanged; removing the abstract's release sentence does not remove access information because the front-page link remains.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands speech-related positioning, discussing paralinguistic information loss, cascaded versus end-to-end systems, and duplex interaction through E-chat, paralinguistics-enhanced language modeling, LLaMA-Omni, Moshi, and the already cited Mini-Omni2. It adds an explicit visual-capability contrast with these systems. Introductory citations also change, including removal of InstructBLIP, Chameleon, MME-Survey, and MME-RealWorld.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction receive localized edits, related work gains a paragraph, and the conclusion becomes 'Conclusion and Future Work.' Impact and acknowledgment sections and revised author/affiliation information are added. Most technical prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are resized, Figure 2's caption is shortened, and Figure 3 is redrawn and enlarged onto a dedicated page. Its Stage 2.2 state-head label and several training-status icons disappear. Tables are resized or relocated, with 'Ours' headings replaced or removed, while their data and basic organization remain intact.

improvement.justification: The expanded speech-related discussion and explicit personalization/memory limitations add useful context without changing the empirical evidence. However, Figure 3 loses annotations retained in the method prose, and Section 2's new claim that the named speech models lack visual capability is difficult to reconcile with its own Mini-Omni2 reference title, which explicitly includes vision. These benefits and new clarity concerns leave the net quality effect uncertain.
